harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel joining node1's (VyOS) private LAN (10.10.1.0/24, hosting node3) and node2's (OPNsense) private LAN (10.10.2.0/24, hosting node4) across their transit link (10.10.12.0/30). Discovered the physical NIC pairings via arping/ping (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 transit; node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0; node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0), assigned static addressing, stood up a WireGuard tunnel (10.10.99.0/30) between the routers with reciprocal AllowedIPs covering each private subnet, added OPNsense filter/interface-assignment and VyOS static-route glue needed for the OPNsense WG plugin's route-derivation quirks, and added specific (non-default-route-clobbering) static routes on node3/node4 pointing at their router for the peer's private subnet. Verified bidirectional host-to-host ping (node3<->node4) traveling only through the tunnel. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (VyOS `reboot`, OPNsense `/sbin/reboot`, RHEL `systemctl reboot`), confirming a changed OS-native boot marker (kernel boot_id / kern.boottime) each time and proving post-restart recovery of interfaces, the WireGuard handshake, static routes, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Mapped topology: node1(VyOS)/node2(OPNsense) routers, node3/node4(RHEL10) hosts, using arping/ping to confirm real NIC pairings across the 3 extra NICs per router vs 1 per host
Configured node1 eth1=10.10.12.1/30 (transit) and eth2=10.10.1.1/24 (LAN1) via VyOS configure/commit/save
Configured node2 opt1=vtnet1=10.10.12.2/30 (transit) and opt2=vtnet2=10.10.2.1/24 (LAN2) by editing /conf/config.xml and configctl interface reconfigure
Added OPNsense filter pass rules for opt1/opt2 (default-deny required explicit allow) via config.xml + configctl filter reload

Set node3 enp8s0=10.10.1.2/24 and node4 enp8s0=10.10.2.2/24 via nmcli, with specific static routes to the peer's private subnet (not a default-route override, to avoid breaking mgmt-network default route)
Generated WireGuard keys on node1 (VyOS PKI) and node2 (wg genkey/pubkey), configured wg0 on node1 (10.10.99.1/30) via VyOS CLI with peer allowed-ips 10.10.99.2/32+10.10.2.0/24

Configured OPNsense WireGuard server/client model directly (config.xml + PHP model validation) since the OPNsense WG plugin derives AllowedIPs from the client's tunneladdress field, not a dedicated allowedips field; rendered/applied via configctl template reload + wireguard start

Diagnosed and fixed an OPNsense reconciler-clobber pattern where assigning wg0 as opt3 with ipaddr=none caused configctl interface reconfigure to strip the WireGuard-assigned tunnel IP; fixed by setting opt3's static ipaddr to match the wg address

Diagnosed missing auto-route for the peer private subnet on both VyOS (Linux wg doesn't auto-install AllowedIPs routes) and OPNsense (peers/UUID matching); added `set protocols static route 10.10.2.0/24 next-hop 10.10.99.2` on VyOS and created a persistent OPNsense Gateway (WG_NODE1 via 10.10.99.1 on opt3) + static Route (10.10.1.0/24) via the PHP model API, applied with rc.routing_configure
Verified bidirectional node3<->node4 ping over the tunnel
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id/kern.boottime + healthy wg/ping state) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time), polling each until reachable again, confirming a changed boot identity, and re-verifying WireGuard handshake, routes, and node3<->node4 connectivity after each restart before proceeding to the next node

evidence.requirement: Private networks joined via WireGuard tunnel between the two routers
evidence.summary: Keys generated on both VyOS(node1) and OPNsense(node2); wg0 interfaces configured with matching pubkeys/allowed-ips; wg show on both sides confirms an established handshake and the interface is up with correct addressing.

evidence.requirement: Hosts (node3, node4) reach each other by their private addresses
evidence.summary: node3 (10.10.1.2) and node4 (10.10.2.2) successfully ping each other with 0% loss in both directions after routing/firewall fixes; earlier commands confirm the physical NIC-to-router pairing used for private LAN addressing.

evidence.requirement: Traffic between routers travels inside the tunnel, not raw across transit
evidence.summary: Routing tables on node1 (10.10.2.0/24 via wg0) and node2 (10.10.1.0/24 via wg0/10.10.99.1) show the only path to the peer's private subnet is through the WireGuard interface, not the raw transit link.

Baseline boot_id 2674ee60...; reboot issued; node unreachable during restart; post-restart boot_id f9775a5b... (changed); interfaces, wg0 handshake, and static route to 10.10.2.0/24 all recovered; node3->node4 ping still succeeds.

Baseline kern.boottime 05:25:54; reboot issued via /sbin/reboot; SSH unreachable during restart; post-restart kern.boottime 05:42:48 (changed); wg0/tunnel address, wg handshake, and static route to 10.10.1.0/24 auto-recovered from config.xml; node4->node3 ping succeeds.

Baseline boot_id 4ebdfa06...; systemctl reboot issued; unreachable during restart; post-restart boot_id 61a6f50c... (changed); enp8s0 static IP and route to 10.10.2.0/24 persisted via NetworkManager profile; ping to node4 succeeds.

Baseline boot_id 646e5f74...; systemctl reboot issued; unreachable during restart; post-restart boot_id 132e264a... (changed); enp8s0 static IP and route to 10.10.1.0/24 persisted; ping to node3 succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Final cross-node verification after all four restarts
evidence.summary: After all four sequential restarts, node3<->node4 ping succeeds with 0% loss and both routers show an active, recent WireGuard handshake on wg0.
